note: Pilot briefs only. Every item is needs_research. No source is verified. Not runnable content: see SCHEMA.md compatibility section.

scenarios.title: The Third Missed Deadline
scenarios.core_tension: The manager must address a repeated missed deadline without assuming the cause is effort when scope or support may be involved.
scenarios.summary: A team member has missed three consecutive delivery dates. The manager has not yet asked what changed.
scenarios.employee_behaviour_pattern: Quiet on status updates until after the date passes.
scenarios.manager_objective: Agree a realistic plan and an early-warning routine.
scenarios.manager_own_contribution: Targets were set in a planning session the employee did not attend.

evidence_pack_outline.observed: Three due dates passed in eight weeks.
Dates were agreed without the employee present.

scenarios.scoring_notes: Criteria: names observed dates, asks about causes, agrees specific next steps, acknowledges own planning role.

boundaries.learner_may_practise: Describing observed dates, asking open questions, agreeing steps.
must_not_do: speculate about causes not in evidence

research_questions: What does evidence say about behaviour-based versus trait-based feedback on later performance?
What does UK guidance recommend for informal performance conversations before any formal process?
What is known about how unclear expectations contribute to missed deadlines?

scenarios.title: The Same Disagreement Again
scenarios.core_tension: The manager must address a recurring public disagreement between two colleagues without taking a side or silencing legitimate task disagreement.
scenarios.summary: Two senior team members repeatedly disagree in team meetings about priorities. Others have stopped contributing.
scenarios.employee_behaviour_pattern: Challenges a peer's proposals directly and at length in group settings.
scenarios.manager_objective: Separate the legitimate disagreement from the manner, and agree how disagreements are raised.
scenarios.manager_own_contribution: The team has no agreed way to settle priority conflicts.

evidence_pack_outline.observed: Disagreement on priorities in four of five meetings.
Two members report holding back.

scenarios.scoring_notes: Criteria: separates task from manner, avoids taking sides, names the impact on others, proposes a process change.

boundaries.learner_may_practise: Naming impact, separating issues, proposing a process.
must_not_do: speculate about causes not in evidence

research_questions: What does evidence say about task conflict versus relationship conflict in teams?
What do published conflict-handling or mediation frameworks recommend for recurring public disagreement?
What does psychological-safety research support and not support about manager responses to dissent?

scenarios.title: When Is My Promotion?
scenarios.core_tension: The manager must be honest about uncertain promotion timing without creating false hope or discouraging a strong performer.
scenarios.summary: A high performer asks for a promotion date. The manager does not control the decision or its timing.
scenarios.employee_behaviour_pattern: Direct and hopeful; has begun comparing themselves with peers.
scenarios.manager_objective: Be clear on what is known, unknown and in the manager's control, and agree development steps.
scenarios.manager_own_contribution: The manager once implied the review would happen this year.

evidence_pack_outline.observed: Two consecutive strong ratings.
evidence_pack_outline.not_proven: That promotion is warranted or scheduled.

evidence_pack_outline.observed: Promotion round dates not yet confirmed.
evidence_pack_outline.not_proven: Whether the employee will be considered.

likely_outcomes: Shared understanding of criteria and timing
scenarios.scoring_notes: Criteria: does not promise outcomes, states unknowns, owns the earlier implication, agrees concrete development steps.

boundaries.learner_may_practise: Clarifying criteria, naming unknowns, agreeing development steps.

research_questions: What does evidence say about vague promotion timelines and trust or retention?
What UK guidance exists on fairness in promotion and progression decisions?
What does research on developmental feedback support, and in what settings?

scenarios.title: Gone Quiet After the Restructure
scenarios.core_tension: The manager must understand a change in engagement after a restructure without presuming burnout, disloyalty or a particular cause.
scenarios.summary: A previously active team member has become withdrawn since the team was reorganised.
scenarios.employee_behaviour_pattern: Fewer contributions in meetings, camera off, shorter replies.
scenarios.manager_objective: Invite the employee's view of the change and agree what support or clarity would help.
scenarios.manager_own_contribution: Changes were announced by email with little discussion.

evidence_pack_outline.observed: Contributions dropped after the reorganisation.
Two 1:1s shortened by the employee.

likely_outcomes: Employee says nothing is wrong, door left open
Workload or role clarity issue found
scenarios.scoring_notes: Criteria: states observations, asks open questions, avoids diagnosing, acknowledges how the change was communicated.

boundaries.learner_may_practise: Describing observations, inviting views, offering support options.
must_escalate: Signs of serious distress: signpost to wellbeing and HR routes
must_not_do: assume the restructure is the cause

research_questions: What is known about disengagement after restructuring and how it differs from burnout?
What does self-determination research say about managerial support after disruption?
What does evidence say about how employees interpret limited communication during change?

scenarios.title: The Manager Who Keeps Everything
scenarios.core_tension: The manager must recognise that their own over-retention of work is holding the team back, and discuss it with a team member who wants more responsibility.
scenarios.summary: A capable team member says they are under-used. The manager has been taking the interesting work.
scenarios.employee_behaviour_pattern: Polite but disengaging; asks for more varied work.
scenarios.manager_objective: Reframe the conversation around delegating a real piece of work with clear decision rights.
scenarios.manager_own_contribution: The manager has retained high-visibility tasks.

evidence_pack_outline.observed: Last six major tasks all held by the manager.
Employee asked for stretch work twice.
evidence_pack_outline.not_proven: What stretch work would suit them.

likely_outcomes: A delegated task with clear authority
scenarios.scoring_notes: Criteria: acknowledges own pattern, sets clear decision rights, agrees support and check-ins.

boundaries.learner_may_practise: Reflecting on own pattern, setting decision rights.
must_not_do: speculate about causes not in evidence

research_questions: What does evidence say about managers over-retaining work and effects on team development?
What delegation frameworks exist and what is their evidential basis versus practitioner origin?
What does research on autonomy and monitoring say about trust after delegation?

scenarios.title: Is My Job Safe?
scenarios.core_tension: The manager must respond honestly to job-security anxiety during a reorganisation when they cannot disclose or do not know the outcome.
scenarios.summary: During a reorganisation under consultation, an employee asks directly whether their job is safe.
scenarios.employee_behaviour_pattern: Anxious, asks repeated direct questions, seeks reassurance.
scenarios.manager_objective: Be truthful about what is known, avoid false reassurance, and point to the formal process and support.

evidence_pack_outline.observed: Consultation open until a stated date.
evidence_pack_outline.not_proven: Who is affected or the outcome.

evidence_pack_outline.observed: Manager told not to discuss selection criteria.

likely_outcomes: Employee informed of process and support
Employee remains anxious but not misled
scenarios.scoring_notes: Criteria: does not speculate or reassure falsely, explains process and support routes, listens.

boundaries.learner_may_practise: Explaining process, listening, naming what is unknown.
must_escalate: Any individual selection or legal question goes to HR

research_questions: What do ACAS or CIPD materials say about communicating during redundancy consultation, and what must a manager avoid saying?
What does research on job insecurity say about effects and manager behaviours studied?
What is known about how people interpret ambiguous communication in restructuring?

scenarios.title: Messages at Midnight
scenarios.core_tension: The manager must address out-of-hours working that the team reads as an expectation, including their own role in setting it.
scenarios.summary: A team member routinely replies to messages late at night, and others are following suit.
scenarios.employee_behaviour_pattern: Replies in the evening and at weekends; says it is a personal choice.
scenarios.manager_objective: Clarify expectations, agree boundaries, and own any signal the manager has sent.
scenarios.manager_own_contribution: The manager sends evening messages and has praised fast replies.

evidence_pack_outline.observed: Frequent replies after 22:00.
Several late evening messages sent by the manager.

likely_outcomes: Employee keeps own pattern by choice
scenarios.scoring_notes: Criteria: acknowledges own signals, distinguishes choice from expectation, agrees explicit norms.

research_questions: What do HSE management standards and ACAS guidance say about workload, working hours and manager responsibilities?
What does evidence say about out-of-hours working expectations and wellbeing?
Which Working Time Regulations provisions are relevant and need legal review?

scenarios.title: A Different Way to Run Meetings
scenarios.core_tension: The manager must respond to an informal request to change meeting formats without asking about or assuming a health condition.
scenarios.summary: An employee asks if meetings can include a written agenda and pauses for response, without giving a reason.
scenarios.employee_behaviour_pattern: Concise, reserved; has not given a reason for the request.
scenarios.manager_objective: Respond constructively, agree a trial of the format, and know when to involve HR for a formal adjustment.

evidence_pack_outline.observed: A request for written agendas and pauses.
Agendas currently shared verbally.

scenarios.scoring_notes: Criteria: no probing for a diagnosis, positive response, offers formal route, confidentiality respected.

boundaries.learner_may_practise: Responding constructively, trialling the format, offering the formal route.
must_escalate: Any formal adjustment request or disclosure of a condition goes to HR/occupational health

research_questions: What do ACAS and the Equality and Human Rights Commission say about reasonable adjustments and informal requests?
What guidance states what a manager must not do when an employee raises a need, such as asking for a diagnosis or sharing information without consent?
What does evidence say about manager responses to disclosure?

scenarios.title: The Numbers Don't Look Right
scenarios.core_tension: The manager must listen to a concern about adjusted figures and route it responsibly without investigating, promising confidentiality they cannot keep, or dismissing it.
scenarios.summary: An employee quietly tells the manager they were asked to adjust figures in a report and they are uncomfortable.
scenarios.employee_behaviour_pattern: Hesitant, worried about consequences, asks that it stay between them.
scenarios.manager_objective: Listen, thank them, explain the escalation route, avoid investigating or promising secrecy, protect against retaliation.

evidence_pack_outline.observed: A request to adjust figures was made.
A raising-concerns policy exists.

likely_outcomes: Employee reassured about process, not outcome
scenarios.scoring_notes: Criteria: listens, does not investigate, does not promise confidentiality, explains escalation, names retaliation protections.

boundaries.learner_may_practise: Listening and explaining the route only.
must_escalate: The concern itself must be passed to the designated route (HR, compliance or whistleblowing contact)
must_not_do: tell the employee the claim is true or false

research_questions: What do UK whistleblowing and public-interest-disclosure sources say about how a manager must respond to a concern?
What does evidence say about retaliation risks and the effect of manager responses on whether concerns are raised?
Which duties are statutory and which are organisational policy?

scenarios.title: Left Out of the Decision
scenarios.core_tension: The manager must address a remote team member's exclusion from decisions made in office conversations without blaming individuals.
scenarios.summary: A remote team member learns about decisions after they are made in the office. They raise it calmly.

context.setting: Hybrid professional-services firm, offices in two time zones

scenarios.employee_behaviour_pattern: Calm, factual, says it keeps happening.
scenarios.manager_objective: Acknowledge the pattern, own the structure that causes it, and agree specific process changes.
scenarios.manager_own_contribution: Quick office decisions are the team's habit and the manager has not challenged them.

evidence_pack_outline.observed: Four of six recent decisions were made in office-only conversations.
Learned of decisions afterwards.

likely_outcomes: Employee appreciates acknowledgement but wants evidence of change
scenarios.scoring_notes: Criteria: acknowledges the pattern, avoids blame, agrees specific, checkable process changes.

boundaries.learner_may_practise: Acknowledging the pattern, agreeing process changes.
must_not_do: speculate about causes not in evidence

research_questions: What does evidence say about inclusion and information access in hybrid teams across locations?
What does research on remote meeting practices support and not support?
What guidance exists for managers on equitable participation in distributed teams?
